questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

Rohit was taught classical music by the most renowned master in the state Sri Sanath Maharaj

options.text: The most renowned master in the state Sri Sanath Maharaj was taught classical music by Rohit.
The most renowned master in the state Sri Sanath Maharaj taught classical music to Rohit.
The classical music Rohit learnt was from the most renowned master in the state Sri Sanath Maharaj.
The most renowned master in the state Sri Sanath Maharaj is teaching classical music to Rohit.

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is** The most renowned master in the state Sri Sanath Maharaj taught classical music to Rohit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **passive voice**. We need to change it into** active voice**.
 
• The object of the passive voice **'The most renowned master in the state Sri Sanath Maharaj'** will become the subject of the active voice.
 
• The subject of the passive voice **'Rohit' **will become the object of the active voice.
 
• The given sentence is in **simple past tense.**
 
• The **structure **of** simple past tense:**
 
 
• Passive Voice: **Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject.**
 
• Active Voice:** Subject + V2 + Object.**
 
 
 
• **'was taught'** changes to **'taught'.**
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

**Correct Active Voice:**__ *The most renowned master in the state Sri Sanath Maharaj taught classical music to Rohit*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

In the introductory session, the teacher asked me __to what district__ I came from.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **which district**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Option 3 is correct because ""which"" is used to refer to a limited number of options or choices, whereas ""what"" is used to refer to an unlimited number of options or choices. In this case, the teacher is asking about a specific district that the speaker came from, so ""which"" is the appropriate word to use.
 
• Option 1 is incorrect because it uses the preposition ""to"" before ""which,"" which is unnecessary and makes the sentence sound awkward.
 
• Option 4 is incorrect because ""what"" implies an unlimited number of options or choices, which is not the case in this sentence.
 
• Option 2 is also incorrect because it does not address the issue of using the correct word to refer to a specific district.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *In the introductory session, the teacher asked me which district__ I came from.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.**

The teacher __corroborated__ the statement of the principal.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Confirmed.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The most appropriate synonym of the underlined word "**corroborated**" is "**confirmed**."
 
• **Corroborated**: supported or confirmed by other evidence; to make more certain.
 
 
• *Example: The witness's testimony **corroborated **the defendant's alibi.*
 
 
 
• **Confirmed**: verified or proved to be true; accepted as valid or final.
 
 
• *Example: The company **confirmed **that the product would be available in stores next month.*
 
 
 
• **Disagreed**: had a different opinion or viewpoint; did not come to an agreement.
 
 
• *Example: The two sides **disagreed **on the terms of the contract.*
 
 
 
• **Disapproved**: had an unfavorable opinion or judgement about something; did not approve of something.
 
 
• *Example: The teacher **disapproved **of the student's behavior in class.*
 
 
 
• **Criticised**: to express disapproval or negative judgement; to find fault with.
 
 
• *Example: The movie was **criticised **for its poor acting and weak storyline.*
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the word "**corroborated**" means that the teacher confirmed the statement of the principal. Therefore, "**confirmed**" is the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in this context.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.**

All eyes turned to him because he was the only person who could __stave off__ the impending war.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Prevent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom **"stave off" **in the given sentence is **"prevent."**
 
• **Stave off: **to prevent or delay something unpleasant or dangerous from happening.
 
 
• Example: Taking vitamin C supplements can help** stave off **colds and flu.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase** "stave off"** is used to describe the action that the person in question could take to prevent the impending war. Therefore, the correct answer is **"prevent."**
 
• **"Prevent" **means to stop something from happening or to avoid something undesirable from occurring.
 
 
• Example: Wearing a helmet while riding a bike can **prevent **head injuries in case of an accident.
 
 
 
• **Option 2, "invoke,"** does not fit the context of the sentence because there is no indication that the person in question is calling upon a higher power or authority for help.
 
• **Option 3, "draw,"** does not fit the context of the sentence because there is no indication that the person in question is attracting or bringing anything closer.
 
• **Option 4, "provoke," **does not fit the context of the sentence because there is no indication that the person in question is inciting a reaction or causing anger.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Invoke: **to call upon a higher power, authority, or spirit for help or inspiration.

 
 
• Example: The priest **invoked **the name of God in his prayer.
 
 
 
• **Draw**: to attract or bring something or someone closer; to cause a particular reaction or response.
 
 
• Example: The new shopping mall **drew **large crowds of shoppers on its opening day.
 
 
 
• **Provoke:** to incite or stimulate a strong reaction or response; to cause anger or annoyance.
 
 
• Example: The athlete's arrogant behavior **provoked **his opponents.

questions.question:
Select the correct superlative degree of comparison for the given sentence.

The money arrived when l (little) expected it.

options.text: The money arrived when I least expected it.
The money arrived when I less expected it.
The money arrived when I little expected it.
The money arrived when I expected it.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **The money arrived when I least expected it**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• 'Least' is correct in this context because it is the **superlative form** of the adjective 'little'.
 
• In this sentence, 'least' is used to indicate the smallest amount of expectation.
 
• It is a comparative form used to compare the level of expectation with other times when the money was expected.
 
• The sentence means that the money arrived at a time when the speaker had the lowest level of expectation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **The money arrived when I least expected it**.

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. A small stream emerged from a cluster of rocks to feed the pool.

B. It was on such a day - a hot, tired day - that Ranji found the pool in the forest.

C. During the monsoon, this stream would be a gushing torrent, cascading down from the hills, but during the summer, it was barely a trickle.

D. The water had a gentle translucency, and you could see the smooth round pebbles at the bottom of the pool.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **BDAC.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph is** BDAC.**
 
• **B** is the first sentence, which introduces the context of the story. It tells the reader about a hot and tired day, on which Ranji finds a pool in the forest. **Sentence D** provides a description of the pool, its clear water, and the round pebbles visible at the bottom of the pool.
 
• **Sentence A** gives information about the source of the pool, which is a small stream emerging from a cluster of rocks. This information is significant in setting the scene and giving the reader a better understanding of the location.
 
• **Sentence C** provides more information about the stream, and how it changes during the monsoon and summer season. This sentence gives additional context to the pool's location, which helps the reader visualize the scene.
 
• Therefore, the correct order of the sentences is **BDAC**, which forms a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 4.**

**Correct Sequence:**

**B.** It was on such a day - a hot, tired day - that Ranji found the pool in the forest.

**D.** The water had a gentle translucency, and you could see the smooth round pebbles at the bottom of the pool.

**A.** A small stream emerged from a cluster of rocks to feed the pool.

**C.** During the monsoon, this stream would be a gushing torrent, cascading down from the hills, but during the summer, it was barely a trickle.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

By whom have the problems been solved?
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Who has solved the problems?**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The above-given sentence is in the **passive voice.**
 
• We need to change it into **active voice**.
 
• We need to follow the given steps for converting the given sentence into active voice:-
 
• In sentences containing** 'who',** the passive starts with **'by whom'.**The following structure is followed:-
 
 
• Passive Voice - By whom + helping verb + Object + V3?
 
• Active Voice - Who + V1 + Object?
 
 
 
• The given sentence is in **present perfect tense.**
 
• **'have been solved' **changes to** 'has solved'.**
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

**Therefore, the correct active voice is** ​*Who has solved the problems?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When we convert **active voice to passive voice,** three things need to be kept in mind:-

 
 
• Change **object **into **subject**.
 
• Change **subject **into **object**.
 
• Always use the **third form of the verb** in the passive voice.
 
• Use **'by'** before the new object. (there are some exceptions to this rule too)

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

They said that they had gone on a vacation.

options.text: They said, "we have been going on a vacation."
They said, "we has gone on a vacation."
They said, "we had been gone on a vacation."
They said, "we have gone on a vacation."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **They said, "we have gone on a vacation."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Option 4 is the correct Direct Speech because it maintains the tense and subject-verb agreement of the original sentence.
 
• The original sentence is in the past tense, with "had gone" indicating a completed action in the past. Option 4 correctly changes "had gone" to "have gone" to reflect the present perfect tense in the Direct Speech.
 
• Additionally, "they" remains the subject in both the reported and direct speech, and "have gone" agrees with the plural subject.
 
• Option 1 is incorrect because it changes the tense to present continuous, which does not match the original sentence. Option 2 is incorrect because it uses the incorrect verb form "has gone" instead of "have gone" for a plural subject. Option 3 is incorrect because it uses the past perfect continuous tense, which is not necessary in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **They said, "we have gone on a vacation."**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.**

He brought these sweets __for you and I.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 4, "for you and me."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The appropriate phrase to substitute is **"for you and me".**
 
• The reason is that **"me" **is the object of the preposition **"for." **
 
• In this sentence,** "me" **is in the objective case because it is the object of the preposition **"for."**
 
 
• Example: He gave the gift to my sister and **me**.
 
 
 
• Thus, an objective pronoun is needed.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

**Correct Sentence:**__ *He brought these sweets __**for you and me**__.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Subjective pronouns** are used as the **subject **of a sentence. They are:

 
 
• I, You, He, She, It, We, They
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• **She **is going to the store.
 
• **We **are having a party tonight.
 
 
 
• **Objective pronouns** are used as the **object **of a sentence. They are:
 
• Me, You, Him, Her, It, Us, Them
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• He gave the book to **me**.
 
• She saw **him **at the park.
 
 
 
• Note that **"it"** is the same for both subjective and objective pronouns.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate idiom or phrase to complete the given sentence.**

I'm not coming to office today, I'm ______.

options.text: feeling a bit under the weather
not playing with the full deck

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Feeling a bit under the weather.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The most appropriate idiom to complete the given sentence is **"feeling a bit under the weather."**
 
• **Feeling under the weather: **to feel ill or unwell.
 
 
• Example: I can't go to the party tonight, I'm **feeling under the weather.**
 
 
 
• **Letting sleeping dogs lie: **to leave a situation alone in order to avoid making it worse.
 
 
• Example: I know my roommate borrowed my shirt without asking, but I'm going to** let sleeping dogs lie **and not say anything.
 
 
 
• **Taking a back seat: **to relinquish control or responsibility; to let others take charge.
 
 
• Example: I'm going to** take a back seat **on this project and let someone else lead the team.
 
 
 
• **Not playing with the full deck: **to be mentally or emotionally unstable or impaired.
 
 
• Example: I don't think we can trust him to make sound decisions, he's **not playing with the full deck.**
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the speaker is informing that they won't be coming to the office because they are feeling unwell. Therefore, the most appropriate idiom is **"feeling a bit under the weather."**
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

Directions: Each item in this section consists of sentences with an underlined word followed by four words or group of words. Select the option that is opposite in meaning to the underlined word and mark your response on the answer sheet accordingly.

Despite the criticism, the government did not __rescind__ the policy.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Reinstate.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The most appropriate antonym of the underlined word** "rescind"** is** "reinstate."**
 
• **Rescind: **to cancel or revoke a decision, order, or agreement. ( रद्द कर देना)
 
 
• Example: The company had to **rescind **its offer of employment due to budget constraints.
 
 
 
• **Revoke: **to officially cancel or annul a law, order, or agreement. (रद्द करना)
 
 
• Example: The court may **revoke **the driver's license of someone found guilty of DUI.
 
 
 
• **Relegate:** to assign someone or something to a lower or less important position, rank, or category.
 
 
• Example: After the merger, some employees were **relegated **to lower positions. (निम्नीकृत करना or पदावनत करना )
 
 
 
• **Rewind:** to wind back or turn back to an earlier position or time.
 
 
• Example: You can **rewind **the video to watch the scene again. (पीछे मोड़ना)
 
 
 
• The given sentence talks about the government not cancelling or revoking a policy despite criticism. Therefore, the most appropriate antonym of **"rescind"** would be **"reinstate,"** which means **to restore or bring back into effect.**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4, "reinstate."**
